questions.cardText:
[Physics] Which of the following accelerates the fastest?
A. A flea jumping
B. A space shuttle at launch
C. A frog darting out its tongue
Answer: A. Fleas can achieve accelerations up to 100 times the force of gravity (100g) while a frog darting out its tongue can achieve accelerations over 10g. A space shuttle at launch can accelerate at about 3g during liftoff.
questions.de: Welches flügellose, blutsaugende Insekt hält beim Springen Beschleunigungen von etwa dem Hundertfachen der Erdanziehung (100 g) aus?
questions.en: Which wingless, blood-sucking insect withstands accelerations of about 100 times the force of gravity (100 g) when it jumps?

timeline.labelEn: Bennet-Clark and Lucey film jumping fleas and propose the resilin spring behind their leap
timeline.labelDe: Bennet-Clark und Lucey filmen springende Flöhe und schlagen die Resilin-Feder als Antrieb ihres Sprungs vor

source.title: Fleas' Feet Unleash That Spectacular Leap (Carl Zimmer, The New York Times, 2011)

questions.notes: The 'fastest' comparison holds only among the card's options: the froghopper out-jumps the flea (Wikipedia, Flea). Estimates vary: ~100 g is the classic figure; analysis of Sutton & Burrows' 2011 high-speed footage gives ~150 g.

questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] In Japan, which restaurant’s food is traditionally eaten at Christmas?
A. KFC B. McDonald’s C. Pizza Hut
Answer: A. This tradition started from a successful marketing campaign by KFC in the 1970s and since then eating KFC fried chicken has become a widespread practice in Japan during Christmas.
questions.de: Das Brathähnchen welcher Fast-Food-Kette wird in Japan dank einer Werbekampagne aus den 1970er-Jahren traditionell zu Weihnachten gegessen?
questions.en: Which fast-food chain's fried chicken is traditionally eaten at Christmas in Japan, thanks to a 1970s marketing campaign?

timeline.labelEn: KFC Japan launches its nationwide "Kentucky for Christmas" campaign
timeline.labelDe: KFC Japan startet seine landesweite Kampagne „Kentucky zu Weihnachten“

questions.notes: Store manager Takeshi Okawara began promoting party barrels as a Christmas meal in 1970; the nationwide campaign followed in 1974.
